problem: Existing treatments were not reaching the most dependent users.
title: Switzerland prescribes medical heroin to heavily dependent users
context: Switzerland had open drug scenes and many heavily dependent users involved in crime.
decision_made: Prescribe heroin under medical supervision, initially to 1,000 users and later up to 3,000.
action_taken: Evaluated retention, crime, health and deaths, with a six-year follow-up cohort of 366 participants.
observed_outcome: Evaluations found large reductions in illicit drug use and drug-related crime, no fatal overdoses of the prescribed drug, and retention of 89 percent at six months. Some figures come from the programme's own researchers.
lessons: Medical prescription can retain very dependent users in treatment and reduce related harm.
limitations: Start year differs by source, the follow-up is a single cohort, and evaluations were not designed to measure effects on drug markets. Several sources are from advocates and programme researchers.

claims.claim_text: Switzerland introduced heroin prescription for heavily dependent users in the 1990s.
A six-year follow-up evaluated the long-term effects of heroin-assisted treatment in Switzerland.
